## PRESEPTAL CELLULITIS
Preseptal cellulitis involves soft tissues in front of the orbital septum and
the eyelids and is often preceded by sinusitis. Infection does not involve the
orbital contents. The most common pathogenic organisms in adults are
streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus aureus.
Treat under the guidance of ophthalmology and/or otolaryngology. Intravenous
antimicrobials are indicated initially for treatment of moderate to severe
disease. Switch to oral antimicrobials when the patient's symptoms improve and
the patient can tolerate oral medications.
## Moderate to severe infection or failure of oral antibiotics
Transition to oral antibiotics can be considered if significant improvement
within 24-48 hours.
Preferred:
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] for 5 days
## Treatment of mild disease or step-down treatment after initial intravenous
## therapy. Treat for a total duration of 5 days.
Preferred:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID ($) [R] < AND>
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days
Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] <AND> trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO
BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days
